task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0771-tenant-migration-replay-on-deploy.md exactly, gated PASS by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (see step-02-code-design-validator.json's result). Implement all of section 2: (2.1) Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_all_pending/0 added to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex; (2.2) new module Letflow.TenantProvisioning.MigrationReplayBoot at lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/migration_replay_boot.ex; (2.3) wire MigrationReplayBoot as a new child in lib/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure.ex's init/1 children list, positioned exactly as specified (immediately after {Ecto.Migrator, ...}, before Letflow.Oidc.ProviderRegistry), NOT gated by skip_migrations?(). Follow section 3's idempotency guarantee and section 4's two-layer per-tenant isolation guarantee (sequential Enum + rescue at each call site, plus the existing rescue inside replay_migrations/2 -- do not use Task.async_stream). Follow the logging behavior in 2.2 exactly: a Logger line per failing tenant naming tenant_id, schema_name, and reason, plus one always-logged summary line after the loop (N ok, M failed) including the healthy 0-failed case. MigrationReplayBoot.start_link/1 must always return :ignore, never propagate a crash, exactly as section 2.2/3 state. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate also recorded one MINOR non-gating documentation issue in the design doc (Ecto.Migrator.run/4 raises on failure and returns a bare list on success -- the {:ok, _} wrap is replay_migrations/2's own, not Migrator.run's) -- this does not require a design amendment, just make sure your implementation does not rely on a mistaken belief that Migrator.run/4 itself returns {:ok, _}. After implementing: run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted and quote the real output -- do not claim success without running them.
acceptance_criteria: replay_all_pending/0 exists with the exact @spec from design section 2.1, calls list_registrations/0 and replay_migrations/2 per tenant, returns %{ok: [...], error: [...]}

Per-tenant failure isolation: one tenant's rescue does not prevent iteration over the remaining tenants (both replay_migrations/2's own existing rescue AND a second rescue at replay_all_pending/0's own call site)
mix compile --warnings-as-errors passes, real output quoted in result.summary
mix format --check-formatted passes, real output quoted in result.summary
No new supervised process per tenant (no Task.async_stream, no per-tenant GenServer/Supervisor child)

result.summary: Implemented design doc iss0771-tenant-migration-replay-on-deploy.md section 2 exactly. (2.1) Added Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_all_pending/0 to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex -- calls list_registrations/0, replay_migrations/2 per tenant, accumulates into %{ok: [tenant_id], error: [{tenant_id, reason}]}, with a per-call-site rescue (Layer 2) tagging unrescued exceptions as {:unexpected_exception, exception}, independent of replay_migrations/2's own existing rescue (Layer 1). Sequential Enum.reduce, no Task.async_stream, no per-tenant process. (2.2) Added new module Letflow.TenantProvisioning.MigrationReplayBoot at lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/migration_replay_boot.ex -- not a GenServer/Supervisor, start_link/1 calls replay_all_pending/0 inside an outer try/rescue that itself can never propagate, logs Logger.warning/1 per failing tenant (tenant_id, schema_name looked up from the Registration list already in hand, reason), logs one Logger.info/1 summary line after the loop always (including 0-failed case), and always returns :ignore. (2.3) Wired Letflow.TenantProvisioning.MigrationReplayBoot into lib/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure.ex's init/1 children list immediately after the {Ecto.Migrator, ...} child and before Letflow.Oidc.ProviderRegistry, unconditionally (not behind skip_migrations?()). Also updated the module's moduledoc children-list enumeration (was stale at 19, now 20) and the two ordering-guarantee comments that referenced child indices/total-child-count by position, plus the inline comment on the Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor child, so the moduledoc stays accurate rather than silently stale. Real commands run in this worktree after `mix deps.get` (deps were missing in the fresh worktree, fetched successfully, no network issue): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- compiled all deps and the letflow app cleanly, only warnings emitted were pre-existing ones inside dependency source (eqrcode's encode.ex bitstring-pin warnings, a deprecated mix.exs xref option warning) -- none in lib/letflow/, command exited 0. `mix format --check-formatted` -- exited 0, no output (all files formatted).
